/itineraryStops/4/name.tm: Обед (местный ресторан рядом с Хэундэ или Мипхо)

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/0.source_en: Walk from Mipo station to restaurant (~5 min)

/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The natural break between the coast and the villages.** The capsule ride ends at Mipo at lunchtime, and Haeundae's food streets are a short walk from the station — no extra driving to reach a good meal. Fueling up here sets up the afternoon's two hillside villages, where the walking is at its most vertical.

/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en: About a 45-minute lunch near Mipo/Haeundae right after the Sky Capsule arrives. Typical guide-recommended options: **dwaeji-gukbap (돼지국밥)** — Busan's signature pork-broth rice soup born in the Korean-War refugee era (~₩10,000), **milmyeon** cold wheat noodles, or a harborside seafood table. Lunch is not included (≈ ₩10,000–15,000), so you can pick what suits your appetite and budget.

/itineraryStops/5/timeUsed/0.source_en: Walk onto the sand from Mipo (~5 min)

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/0.source_en: **Korea's most famous beach** — ~1.5 km of sand, FREE and open 24h

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/1.source_en: Marine City skyline backdrop from the water's edge

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/2.source_en: Dongbaekseom island and Nurimaru APEC House at the far west end

/itineraryStops/5/highlights/3.source_en: Directly at Mipo, where the Sky Capsule ride ends — no extra transfer

/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: The capsule lands at Mipo, which is the beach's eastern end — so Busan's most famous view is a five-minute walk away and costs the day nothing. It is deliberately short: enough to stand on the sand and photograph the skyline before the afternoon turns to the hillside villages.

/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
**Haeundae Beach (해운대해수욕장)** is Korea's best-known stretch of sand — about **1.5 km** of shoreline curving between Dongbaekseom island at the west end and Mipo at the east, backed by the Marine City skyline. The Sky Capsule sets you down at Mipo, which is simply the eastern end of this beach, so the stop costs the day no extra driving.

Twenty minutes is a photo-and-toes stop, not a swim: walk out onto the sand, shoot the skyline, and rejoin the coach. In July and August the beach is at its busiest and the parasol rows are up; the rest of the year it is wide, quiet and walkable. Free, open at all hours.

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Flat sand and a paved promenade

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/0.source_en: Coach drop-off at Public Parking Lot 2 + walk to entrance (~5 min)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/1.source_en: Tourist Information Center + Stamp Map purchase (~10 min)
/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/1.tm: Туристический информационный центр и покупка карты для штампов (~10 мин)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/2.source_en: Sky Garden viewpoint + Little Prince bench (~25 min)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/3.source_en: Alley walk past murals + small cafe pause (~25 min)

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/0.source_en: **'Korea's Machu Picchu' / 'Korea's Santorini'** — UN-HABITAT Asian Townscape Award 2012
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/0.tm: **«Корейский Мачу-Пикчу» / «корейский Санторини»** — премия UN-HABITAT Asian Townscape Award 2012

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/1.source_en: Origins: **1920s-1930s** Busan administration relocation + **1955 Taegeukdo refugees** (~800 families)

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.source_en: **Taegeukdo philosophy of 'allowing others to prosper'** = no house blocks the view behind it
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.tm: **Философия Тхэгыкто «дать процветать другим»** — ни один дом не закрывает вид тому, что стоит за ним

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/3.source_en: **2009 'Dreaming of Machu Picchu' + 2010 'Miro Miro'** Ministry of Culture public-art projects
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/3.tm: Проекты общественного искусства Министерства культуры **«Dreaming of Machu Picchu» 2009 года и «Miro Miro» 2010 года**

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/4.source_en: **'Little Prince and Fox' bench** at Sky Garden — the village's most-photographed spot
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/4.tm: **Скамейка «Маленький принц и лис»** в Sky Garden — самое фотографируемое место деревни

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.source_en: **~1.4 million visitors annually** since the public-art revitalization
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.tm: **~1,4 млн посетителей в год** после обновления с помощью общественного искусства

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.source_en: **Living residential community** — quiet voices, no drones, no flash into homes
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.tm: **Здесь живут люди** — говорите тихо, не запускайте дроны и не снимайте со вспышкой в сторону домов

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/7.source_en: Free village entry; optional Stamp Map ~₩2,000
/itineraryStops/6/highlights/7.tm: Вход в деревню бесплатный; карта для штампов по желанию ~₩2 000

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/8.source_en: **UN-HABITAT Asian Townscape Award 2012** — recognition of the 2009 'Dreaming of Machu Picchu' art project that transformed the 1955 Taegeukdo refugee settlement into Busan's signature mural village

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Residents live here — keep voices down, no drones, take rubbish with you; wear grippy shoes for the steep lanes; afternoon golden hour ~16:00-17:00 is the village's best light

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Hanbok rental, craft workshops, Korean candy stalls, cafes; small village museum at the entrance; the stamp map is the easiest way to navigate
/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.tm: Прокат ханбока, ремесленные мастерские, лавки с корейскими сладостями, кафе; у входа небольшой музей деревни; проще всего ориентироваться по карте для штампов

/itineraryStops/6/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The afternoon's headline village — Busan's pastel amphitheater.** After the coastal morning, the day crosses to the west hillsides where Gamcheon's Korean-War-era refugee terraces, reborn as an art village in 2009, stack in candy colors above the sea. The 90-minute loop covers the viewpoints, the Little Prince ledge, and time to wander the alleys — and it pairs deliberately with quiet Dakbatgol just after, so you see both the famous village and the local one the buses skip.

/itineraryStops/6/convenience/restroom.source_en: Public restrooms at the Tourist Information Center and around the main viewpoints
/itineraryStops/6/convenience/restroom.tm: Общественные уборные в туристическом информационном центре и у основных смотровых площадок
